Preferred: resolve the owning project with a non-locking read (select(Stream.project_id).where(Stream.stream_id == stream_id)), check access on that, and only then take the locking read for the actual transition - a DB failure in the guard then happens outside the locked window. primary_findings.title: batch guard DB failure skips the rollback and poisons the rest of the batch
primary_findings.why_it_matters: The new project guard (has_project_access) is a database call inside _submit_one_inner. When it raises, _submit_one's blanket `except Exception` turns it into an INTERNAL_ERROR failed item - but nothing rolls the session back, so the transaction stays open with the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE row lock still held. The transition path has exactly this rollback (stream_batch_service.py:363) and the existing test test_db_level_failure_does_not_poison_the_rest_of_the_batch only covers that path. After one guard failure the session is poisoned: on PostgreSQL the transaction is aborted, so every later item in the batch fails too and the row locks accumulate - which breaks the batch's own 'one item's failure must not affect the others' contract.

The SPEC is the UI's single source of truth, so a frontend implementer reading section 5.4 would still design for a 403 that the API never returns.

residual_risks: The frontend calls `GET /lineage/streams/{id}/graph` (pcs-frontend/src/pages/sim/tabs/StreamLineageTab.tsx) while `data_lineage.record_type` is written as the class name (app/services/lineage.py:109) => the streams lineage tab queries a spelling that never matches and is always empty. Pre-existing, but the new guard registry bakes the same wrong spelling into the security-relevant key set.

callsite completeness: grep-only sweep of `has_project_access` / `check_project_access_or_404` across pcs-backend. Endpoints outside the reviewed files that expose project-scoped records (flash / pipe / vessel / pump result routers) are out of this diff's scope and were not audited; they may still rely on the `check_record_access_or_404` shape ("Project not found: <id>"), which is not byte-identical to a record-level 404.

Every environment now needs a seeding step before the logistics endpoints are usable; CLAUDE.md documents this, but nothing in the code fails loudly when a project has zero UserProject rows (the guard simply 404s for everyone), so a missed seed shows up as an empty frontend rather than an error.

The default pytest `client` fixture monkeypatches UserProjectService.check_user_project_access to always return True, so the ordinary suite cannot detect a missing project guard on any endpoint; only the new `strict_client` fixture exercises the real guard. Nothing enforces that guard tests use strict_client, so a future endpoint tested with `client` can ship unguarded and stay green.

The seed script (pcs-backend/scripts/seed_user_project_access.py) prints raw exception text to stderr (line 170). A malformed-DATABASE_URL failure surfaces in SQLAlchemy as 'Could not parse SQLAlchemy URL from string ...', which can put the DB password into CI logs. Low impact (local ops script, needs DB credentials to run), but the print should be restricted to a safe message.

ensure_user_row creates rows with roles=[] and status=ACTIVE; the real login path (token_issuer.issue_tokens) only writes roles=[role] when it creates the row, and never updates an existing one. A user provisioned by the seed script before their first AD login therefore keeps users.roles == [] permanently, and notification_recipients.py (which treats users.roles as an authoritative input) will stop selecting them.

Mock login (/auth/mock-login) issues a token with an arbitrary role claim for any of four usernames; it is gated by settings.is_production (mock_auth.py:60-66) and the router is not mounted in production, so the ACL model trusting the JWT role claim is acceptable — but this gate is the only thing standing between that trust model and a full auth bypass, so it should stay covered by a production-config assertion.

check_user_project_access ignores the users.status column, so a DISABLED user keeps project access on all newly guarded logistics endpoints. This replicates the pre-existing semantics of check_project_access_or_404, but the logistics surface now depends on that semantics for 20+ endpoints, so the gap is now much wider than before.

create_stream still takes workspace_id from the request body and never verifies that the workspace belongs to the URL's project (pcs-backend/app/api/v1/streams.py:313). A user with access to project A can attach a stream to project B's workspace. Pre-existing, but the logistics surface now enforces project membership everywhere else, so this is now the one remaining cross-project write path in this module.

The review-log query uses detail_json->>'transition', which the existing GIN index (jsonb_path_ops) cannot serve, so every call is a full scan of audit_logs. Deliberately deferred by the service docstring (TODO-104); flagged only because the endpoint is now on a user-facing read path rather than an admin-only one.

[demoted from finding] Review-log row key collides on repeat transitions in same second: The frontend rowKey is `${row.transition}-${row.occurred_at}`; two rows of the same transition in the same transaction share audit_logs.occurred_at (server_default=now()) and collide as React keys. The backend already orders by (occurred_at, audit_id) but does not expose audit_id.

CLAUDE.md 新增段落与 SPEC V2.11 都写「任何没有 UserProject 授权行的用户访问任何物流端点都 404」，但 `POST /streams/batch-submit` 实际返回 207（Multi-Status），跨项目条目以 `reason=SIM_STREAM_NOT_FOUND` 的 failed 项表达（pcs-backend/app/services/stream_batch_service.py:284-297）。枚举向量本身仍被守住（failed 项与真不存在逐字同形），但「都 404」这句在批次端点上不成立 —— 属文档口径过宽，未单列为发现（影响低）。

本批未改 `alembic/versions` 与 ORM 模型 ⇒ 发布前检查里的 `alembic check`（两库各 exit 0）与 `check_migration_idempotency.py` 对本批属 N/A；.gstack/qa-reports/qa-report-pcs-frontend-2026-11-09-stream-guard.md 只记了 pytest / pytest_pg / typecheck / lint / 前端 vitest / 契约 G-08 / 裸载荷 71 这几项，未逐条对照「发布前检查（必做）」清单。

CLAUDE.md 声称的 dev 前置（alice/bob/carol/dan 靠 seed 脚本拿授权）在本地未实测：seed 脚本用 derive_user_id(username) 派生 user_id，而 current_actor 优先取 JWT 的 user_id 声明（app/api/v1/auth.py:38-42）—— 两处当前都落在 uuid5(NAMESPACE_DNS, username) 上，故一致；但若将来 JWT 的 user_id 声明与 uuid5 派生分叉，seed 的授权行会挂到 actor 不认的 user_id 上 ⇒ 用户仍全站 404。

The `strict_client` fixture's strictness is a single-point patch: it restores exactly one accessor, `UserProjectService.check_user_project_access` (tests/conftest.py:280-285). Every guard added by this batch was verified to route through it (`app/api/v1/streams.py:246,274`, `app/api/v1/lineage.py:203`, `app/services/stream_batch_service.py:284` all call `has_project_access`, which calls that accessor), so today the fixture is sound — but no test asserts that property, so a future guard implemented with a direct `UserProject` query or with a client-supplied project id would be invisible to both `client` and `strict_client`.

`_ORIGINAL_CHECK_ACCESS` is captured at conftest import time (tests/conftest.py:280). Any test module that patches `UserProjectService.check_user_project_access` at import time would be captured as "the original" and permanently restored by `strict_client`. `tests/services/report/test_style_service.py:209-230` patches the same attribute (at runtime, restoring by assigning back a bound method rather than the classmethod descriptor) — harmless today, but it leaves the class attribute in a different shape for subsequent tests.

`list_review_log` selects `detail_json->>'transition'`-style JSON path access, which SQLAlchemy compiles differently for PostgreSQL JSONB and SQLite. The unit lane therefore does not prove the query behaves identically on PostgreSQL 18, and the `pg` lane (5 tests) does not cover the review-log endpoint — a PG-only query error would only surface at runtime.

Unit tests run on in-memory SQLite where foreign keys are not enforced. The new `grant_project` fixture works around this by calling `ensure_user_row` first, and `tests/api/v1/test_project_owner_access.py` asserts the `users` row exists, but any future test that writes a `UserProject` row without that helper will be locally green and PG-fatal.

Guard coverage is applied by manual `await _load_stream_guarded(...)` calls inside each endpoint body (8 call sites in streams.py); nothing enforces that a newly added logistics endpoint includes one, and the legacy `client` fixture mocks the guard to always-True, so a missing guard call is invisible to the default suite. A router-level FastAPI dependency would make the guard structural rather than a per-endpoint convention (kept out of the findings: boundary placement is a judgment call, anchor 50).

callsite completeness: grep-only. I verified that the only construction site of `DataLineage` under app/ is app/services/lineage.py:108 and that nothing writes record_type='streams'; a dynamically or string-keyed writer would not have been found by grep, so the F2 claim rests on text search rather than exhaustive coverage.

The `strict_client` fixture restores the guard by process-global assignment; I did not audit every test file for mixed `client` / `strict_client` usage, so the blast radius of the order-dependent semantics is unquantified.

[demoted from finding] SYSTEM_ADMIN bypass rule duplicated in two helpers: SYSTEM_ADMIN bypass and the UserProject lookup are copied between user_project_service.has_project_access and app/api/v1/_guard.py::check_project_access_or_404; the service docstring claims the two 'will not drift', which duplicated code cannot guarantee. Single-reviewer maintainability P2 with no current consequence - a change to one copy would silently diverge the logistics surface from the rest of the API.

[demoted from finding] Two competing guard modes implemented by global class mutation: strict_client implements 'the real guard' by rebinding UserProjectService.check_user_project_access process-wide before every request; the strict/loose choice is invisible at the call site, and the global mutation's blast radius across a mixed client/strict_client suite was not audited.

audit_logs has no implemented retention or partitioning - the monthly-partition plan appears only in a migration docstring (pcs-backend/alembic/versions/p7_s1_002_audit_logs_jsonb_gin.py:13) - so the scan cost of the review-log query grows monotonically with usage; actual production row counts are unknown (dev DB: 12 audit_logs rows, 0 RECORD_TRANSITION, 0 streams).

The same unindexed resource_id lookup shape exists in pre-existing code (pcs-backend/app/api/v1/audit.py:63, pcs-backend/app/api/v1/records_actions.py:449); if the composite index from the P2 finding is added those paths get faster too, but their behaviour and impact were not measured in this review.

audit_logs.occurred_at is server_default=now() (transaction timestamp), so rows written in one transaction share a timestamp; the review-log ORDER BY (occurred_at, audit_id) breaks ties by a random UUIDv4, so intra-transaction ordering is arbitrary rather than insertion order. The frontend rowKey (transition-occurred_at) can therefore collide for two rows in the same transaction.

Guarded single-object endpoints (PATCH/DELETE /streams/{id}, POST /streams/{id}/properties/estimate, the six transition endpoints) now perform one extra db.get plus one user_projects SELECT per request. The re-read of the stream by StreamService.get/update is free (identity map hit via db.get), so no duplicated row load was found; the two added round trips are on paths that already commit, so their latency share is small and was not measured.

[demoted from finding] batch guard adds one SELECT per item inside row lock: The batch guard adds one UserProject SELECT per item (N+1 over up to 100 items per batch); the per-item commit cost the module already accepts dominates it, so no measurement was taken.
`operator` 语义上就是审计里的 user_id（schema 描述已写明），但前端「操作人」列直接渲染这个 UUID ⇒ 页面上是一串 UUID 而非人名；契约没骗人，但可读性有落差。

The seed script pcs-backend/scripts/seed_user_project_access.py has no statement timeout and no confirmation prompt before writing to a real database; a hung database makes the CLI hang indefinitely rather than fail fast.

[demoted from finding] Review-log query unbounded and unindexed on audit_logs: list_review_log applies no row cap, so a pathological stream could produce an unbounded response; the existing GET /audit-logs caps at 200. Not material today (a stream has a handful of review transitions), but the cap is cheap to add.
testing_gaps: No test covers the guard/authorization path for the auto-granted creator after `POST /projects` (tests/api/v1/test_project_owner_access.py asserts the DB rows but never exercises a guarded endpoint with that principal), so a mismatch between the granted user_id and the JWT-derived actor id would not be caught.

No test asserts that the state-transition endpoints return the guard's 404 rather than the composition-gate 422 for a cross-project stream on all six transitions; only the single-stream path shape is asserted today.

`POST /streams/batch-submit` with `dry_run=true` against a cross-project stream is not covered: the guard does run before the dry-run early return in `_submit_one_inner`, but nothing asserts that a dry run reports a foreign stream as `SIM_STREAM_NOT_FOUND` rather than `succeeded`.

The seed script's CLI surface is untested: invalid `--role` (exit 2), malformed `--project` UUID (exit 2), nonexistent project (exit 2), and `--dry-run` writing nothing. Only the inner `seed_user_project_access()` function is covered, yet the script is the documented per-environment deployment prerequisite.

The new `GET /streams/{id}/review-log` endpoint has no OpenAPI contract assertion (that the response is a bare array of `{transition, operator, occurred_at, detail}`); the shape is pinned only by the Python test and the frontend MSW mock, so a backend/frontend contract drift would not be caught by `check_openapi_payload_coverage.py`.

No test asserts that the guarded 404 envelope stays byte-identical to `StreamService.get`'s PcsError envelope after the service's message changes; the current assertions compare the guarded path only against itself.

No PG-lane coverage of the review-log query: the unit tests run on in-memory SQLite where @> is unavailable and JSONB operator/index behaviour differs, so scripts/pytest_pg.sh does not exercise the real ->> extraction or the index usability of this query against PostgreSQL.

No test covers a DB-level failure inside the NEW guard path (`has_project_access` inside `_submit_one_inner`): the existing test `test_db_level_failure_does_not_poison_the_rest_of_the_batch` (tests/services/test_stream_batch_service.py:708) only exercises the transition/audit-write failure path, which has the `await db.rollback()` that the guard path lacks. A test that makes the guard's SELECT fail and asserts that the following item still succeeds would pin the invariant.

triage_groups.title: Lineage guard fails open for some record types
triage_groups.context: Both land on the lineage guard introduced in T5: the missing-record path answers 200 [] instead of the same 404, and the hand-maintained registry skips every record type it does not list.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Decide once which record types are intentionally unguarded (a type with no project_id), then make the guard fail closed for everything else and derive the registry from the canonical record-type vocabulary - handle #6's design decision first, then #1's missing-record path.
triage_groups.why: Both are the same defect class as the hole this batch closes: an unauthorized caller can tell 'exists' from 'does not exist'. #1 is a live oracle today; #6 is the trap that reopens it as soon as a second record type is tracked.

triage_groups.title: Review-log contract drifts from what the state machine writes
triage_groups.context: The new endpoint, its OpenAPI schema and the frontend mock each carry their own hand-written copy of the audit action / transition vocabulary, and the copies disagree with TRANSITION_AUDIT_ACTION.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Derive the action filter and the transition vocabulary from the canonical enums (#2, then #4 - same derivation, one edit), then rebuild the MSW mock from the contract (#5).
triage_groups.why: One derivation removes the endpoint defect, the contract gap and the mock drift at once; the mock must be last or it re-encodes the wrong shape.

triage_groups.title: Batch project guard runs inside the row lock
triage_groups.context: In the batch path the access check happens after SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, so a rejected item still holds a lock and a failing check leaves the session poisoned.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Restructure the guard to run on a non-locking read before the lock is taken (#3 first - the poisoned session breaks the batch's partial-success contract, #9 is the side channel that the same restructuring closes).
triage_groups.why: Both consequences of one placement decision; doing the check before the lock closes the failure window and the cross-tenant lock together.

triage_groups.title: POST /projects auto-grant is not identity-safe, atomic, or race-free
triage_groups.context: The new creator auto-grant path (T0) grants against a row that ensure_user_row may have substituted, in a helper that commits internally, through a lock-free get-or-create with no savepoint.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Make ensure_user_row's identity explicit (#10), apply the repository's savepoint + re-read-winner recipe to both get-or-create helpers (#11), then give create_project a single commit point (#7).
triage_groups.why: All three live in the same create_project / ensure_user_row path; #10 and #11 edit the same function and should be done together, and #7 changes how that path commits.
